title: Choosing the correct household safety statement
question: Consider these statements: 1. A fuse is placed in live to interrupt the live supply during an overcurrent fault. 2. The earth wire carries the normal return current of every metal-bodied appliance. 3. An MCB can be reset after the fault has been investigated and corrected. 4. A neutral-side switch always isolates an appliance from live. Which combination is correct?

options.text: Statements 1 and 2 only.
Statements 2 and 4 only.
Statements 1 and 3 only.
Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4.

explanation: Statement 1 is correct because the fuse should interrupt live. Statement 3 describes a genuine advantage of an MCB. Statement 2 is false because earth should not carry normal operating current, and statement 4 is false because live may remain connected when neutral is switched off.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank

title: Identifying the correct household safety arrangement
question: Two proposed arrangements for a metal-bodied washing machine are shown. In Arrangement P, the switch and fuse are in the live wire, neutral is connected directly to the appliance, and earth connects to the metal casing. In Arrangement Q, the switch is in neutral, the fuse is in earth, and live connects directly to the appliance. <grid columns= gap=> <grid-item> Correct principles </grid-item> <grid-item> Unsafe principles </grid-item> </grid> Which explanation correctly identifies why Arrangement P is safer?

options.text: It places the fuse and switch in live, so switching off or a fuse operation can disconnect the appliance from the live supply, while earth provides a separate protective path for the metal casing.
It makes the earth wire carry normal operating current, which prevents electric shock.
It places the fuse in neutral and the switch in earth, ensuring the appliance receives a constant current.
It allows the appliance's casing to remain live whenever the switch is open, but guarantees that the fuse will never melt.

explanation:
correctly identifies why Arrangement P is safer?

A) It places the fuse and switch in live, so switching off or a fuse operation can disconnect the appliance from the live supply, while earth provides a separate protective path for the metal casing.

B) It makes the earth wire carry normal operating current, which prevents electric shock.

C) It places the fuse in neutral and the switch in earth, ensuring the appliance receives a constant current.

D) It allows the appliance's casing to remain live whenever the switch is open, but guarantees that the fuse will never melt.

**Correct Answer: A**

**Reason:** The live-side fuse protects against excessive current, the live-side switch provides appropriate isolation, and the earth conductor protects exposed metal parts during a fault. Arrangement Q is unsafe because neutral switching may leave the appliance live and fusing the earth conductor can interrupt the protective earth connection.

title: Determining whether a fuse is suitable for a combined load
question: A 220 V circuit supplies a 1,100 W heater, a 440 W iron, and a 220 W fan. A 9 A fuse is fitted. Assume the fuse's specified operating characteristics and wiring are otherwise suitable. Which conclusion follows from the rated load calculation?
diagramSvg: <svg viewBox="0 0 460 190" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="background:#f8fafc; border-radius:8px; border:1px solid #cbd5e1; font-family:system-ui, sans-serif;"><text x="230" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">HOTS Analytical Diagram: Determining whether a fuse is suitable for a combined load</text><rect x="40" y="45" width="380" height="95" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1"/><text x="230" y="72" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#1e40af">High Order Thinking Principles</text><text x="230" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#334155">Refer to the experimental variables and quantitative relationships in the problem</text><text x="230" y="114" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9.5" font-weight="600" fill="#16a34a">Rigorous ICSE Class 10 Syllabus Correlation</text><text x="230" y="165" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" font-weight="600" fill="#64748b">Standard Analytical Schema</text></svg>

options.text: The total current is 7 A, so the fuse is overloaded.
The total current is 8 A, so the normal load is below the 9 A rating.
The total current is 9 A, because the fuse fixes the current at its rating.
The total current is 10 A, so the circuit necessarily has a short circuit.

explanation:
P_{total}=1100+440+220=1760 W



I=(1760 / 220)=8 A


The calculated normal current is below the fuse rating. This does not mean that every 9 A fuse is automatically suitable: its characteristics, the wiring rating, and manufacturer requirements still matter. Option D incorrectly identifies a load calculation as a short circuit.

title: Choosing a fuse for a group of appliances
question: A 220 V circuit supplies a 1,100 W heater, a 660 W iron, and two 110 W fans. All operate simultaneously. The available fuse ratings are 5 A, 8 A, 10 A, and 15 A. Assuming the wiring and manufacturer's specifications permit the choice, what is the smallest listed fuse rating that accommodates the calculated operating current?
diagramSvg: <svg viewBox="0 0 460 190" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="background:#f8fafc; border-radius:8px; border:1px solid #cbd5e1; font-family:system-ui, sans-serif;"><text x="230" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">HOTS Analytical Diagram: Choosing a fuse for a group of appliances</text><rect x="40" y="45" width="380" height="95" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1"/><text x="230" y="72" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#1e40af">High Order Thinking Principles</text><text x="230" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#334155">Refer to the experimental variables and quantitative relationships in the problem</text><text x="230" y="114" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9.5" font-weight="600" fill="#16a34a">Rigorous ICSE Class 10 Syllabus Correlation</text><text x="230" y="165" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" font-weight="600" fill="#64748b">Standard Analytical Schema</text></svg>

options.text: 5 A
8 A

explanation:
Total power:


P=1100+660+2(110)=1980 W


Current:


I=(1980 / 220)=9 A


The 8 A fuse is below the normal load current. The smallest listed rating above 9 A is 10 A. The fuse rating must also protect the wiring and comply with the appliance specifications.

title: Maximum number of heaters on a circuit
question: A household circuit has a 15 A fuse and a 220 V supply. Each heater is rated at 1,100 W. Assume the heaters are identical, operate simultaneously at rated power, and no other appliance is connected. What is the maximum number of heaters that can operate without exceeding the fuse's rated current?
diagramSvg: <svg viewBox="0 0 460 190" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="background:#f8fafc; border-radius:8px; border:1px solid #cbd5e1; font-family:system-ui, sans-serif;"><text x="230" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">HOTS Analytical Diagram: Maximum number of heaters on a circuit</text><rect x="40" y="45" width="380" height="95" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1"/><text x="230" y="72" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="700" fill="#1e40af">High Order Thinking Principles</text><text x="230" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#334155">Refer to the experimental variables and quantitative relationships in the problem</text><text x="230" y="114" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9.5" font-weight="600" fill="#16a34a">Rigorous ICSE Class 10 Syllabus Correlation</text><text x="230" y="165" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" font-weight="600" fill="#64748b">Standard Analytical Schema</text></svg>
explanation:
Current per heater:


I_h=(1100 / 220)=5 A


Maximum number based on the rated current:


n=(15 / 5)=3


Three heaters draw 3×5=15 A. A fourth would draw 20 A and exceed the rating.

**Important:** This is an idealised rating calculation, not a recommendation to design a circuit for continuous operation exactly at the fuse rating. Actual installation design must account for the fuse characteristics, wiring capacity, and applicable standards.
source: ICSE Class 10 Physics HOTS Question Bank
